title: Nodal bucket pricing — sketch
content:
Context / intent:
- Quick personal sketch for a prepaid bucket approach that trades simple UX for predictable revenue and easier unit-econ guarantees to customers. Not a final design; goal is to explore margin bands, expiry, and conversion heuristics so we can show Sales a minimal set of options.

Top-level assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline hosted inference cost to Redwood (amortized infra + ops + model licensing): 0.000012 USD / token (12e-6). This is a blended number across small/medium requests using batching and cache benefits.
- Retail-ish competitive per-token price target we want to expose: 0.00006 USD / token (6e-5) for a baseline PAYG case. That leaves gross margin ~80% on simple stateless calls.
- For interactive/chat (inc. context & KV cache replays) effective token cost ~0.000024 USD / token (24e-6) due to longer lifecycles & memory footprint.
- GPU-hour backcalc: 1 A100-40G equivalent hour => roughly 3.6M generated tokens on average across RLHF-sized models (working assumption). So 1 GPU-hour ≈ 3.6e6 tokens -> cost per GPU-hour variable depending on dedicated/hosted. 
- For committed/dedicated customers we can use lower marginal cost (quantized runtimes, colocated infra): assume 0.000009 USD / token.

Design sketch: Nodal bucket tiers (simple, monotonic):
- Node A: Micro Bucket — $49 up-front -> 1M tokens credit -> effective price = $0.000049 per token. Expiry 90 days. No rollover.
- Node B: Growth Bucket — $299 up-front -> 7M tokens -> effective = $0.0000427 per token. Expiry 180 days. +5% bonus tokens if auto-renew.
- Node C: Scale Bucket — $1999 up-front -> 50M tokens -> effective = $0.00003998 per token. Expiry 365 days. +10% bonus for annual commitment.
- Node D: Enterprise Prepay (quote) -> custom pricing, higher commit, dedicated capacity option, SLA.

Why these numbers?
- Anchor target: want perceived simple prices near 4–6e-5 $/token so customers can do quick math for UX flows (e.g., 10k tokens ~ $0.5).
- Micro bucket purposely priced above baseline PAYG to discourage fragmentation while still giving small users easy onboarding (psychological price point <$50).
- Growth and Scale lower per-token to incentivize volume; bonuses for auto-renew and commit mimic common SaaS discounts.

Unit economics quick checks:
- If micro user burns 1M tokens: revenue = $49, cost (hosted blended 12e-6) = 1e6 * 12e-6 = $12 -> gross margin = $37 (75%). This is acceptable for trial funnel.
- For chat-heavy workloads (effective cost 24e-6): cost = $24 -> margin = $25 -> 51% gross margin. Still OK for starter.
- For Scale bucket at 50M tokens with assumed committed cost 9e-6: cost = 50e6*9e-6 = $450 -> revenue = $1999 -> margin = $1549 (77%). If customer uses our dedicated pool with lower infra cost, margin improves.

Expiry and rollover heuristics:
- Expiry is key for revenue recognition and discouraging hoarding. 90–365 days seems reasonable.
- Soft-rollover option: allow 10% rollover if customer buys next tier within 30 days of expiry. Could be abused; requires guardrails.

Prepay-to-SLA conversion:
- For large enterprise buys, prepay can be converted into guaranteed reserved GPU-hours. Conversion formula: reserved GPU-hours = tokens / tokens_per_gpu_hour (3.6e6). So 50M tokens ≈ 13.9 GPU-hours. That seems low because tokens_per_gpu_hour varies by model/sequence length. Use conservative 2e6 tokens per GPU-hour for long-chains -> 50M / 2e6 = 25 GPU-hours. Clearly we need per-model conversion tables.

Sensitivity table (quick):
- If blended cost rises to 18e-6/token (e.g., model upgrade or longer contexts): Micro margin falls to 63%, Scale margin to ~61%.
- If tokens_per_gpu_hour halves (more expensive inference): enterprise breakpoints should apply a 15–25% surcharge or require larger commit.

UX/Policy considerations (notes to self):
- Offer explicit examples in UI: "Using 10k tokens per month? Micro bucket gives you X months of coverage". Convert tokens to user-facing units (messages, minutes of audio, etc.).
- Show equivalent PAYG price next to bucket price to frame discount.
- Maintain easy top-up flow and immediate consumable credits.
- For refunds/credits: allow prorated refunds if <10% used and within 30 days; otherwise non-refundable. Keeps accounting simple for Sales.

Open questions / risk areas:
- Do we need to map buckets by model family (e.g., Llama2-70B vs instruction-tuned small)? Mixing models with different token->GPU-hour changes economics.
- How to handle streaming burst behavior where small tokens incur overheads? Should we add a min-per-request surcharge for ultra-low token calls?
- Regulatory/compliance: enterprise customers may request evidence of dedicated capacity consumption. Need audit logs mapping tokens->GPU-hours (approx) for invoicing.

Next steps (short actionable):
- Build small spreadsheet with per-model tokens_per_gpu_hour (2e6, 3.6e6, 5e6) and recompute breakpoints for all tiers. Tag models by typical context length.
- Run simulated customer profiles (chat app: 20 messages/user/day, avg 150 tokens/msg) and compute churn sensitivity vs bucket expiry.
- Share with Sales to validate perceived price points (esp $49 micro anchor).

Quick notes to self: keep language simple in product UI, avoid "credits" jargon if customers interpret tokens poorly — show converted units (e.g., "~1M tokens ≈ 6 months of light chat use").

End of slab. This is intentionally rough. Save as reference to iterate — need to reconcile with dedicated SKU math and billing system gating rules before shipping.
